name: m3e-kit
description: Material 3 Expressive implementation kit: everything needed to build the M3 Expressive components on any renderer. All facts derive from the Jetpack Compose Material 3 sources at one androidx commit.
readOrder: foundations.json: system rules every spec assumes (token tiers and modes, units, colour pairing, emphasized type, per-corner shape and morphing, state layers, disabled, focus ring, touch target, spring algorithm, window size classes).
tokens/m3e.resolved.json: every token value, keyed by path. Look up any path a spec names here.
components/<id>.json: one spec per component. Build from its tokenGroups plus its layout, states and behaviour rules; read its notes before trusting a token.
shapes/shapes.json and shapes/morphs.json: only for the shape library and the loading indicator.

conventions.tokenPaths: Strings matching ^(ref|sys|comp)(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+$ are token paths or group prefixes in tokens/m3e.resolved.json; every one in this kit is checked to exist.
conventions.sources: source fields cite Compose as File.kt:line at the pinned commit, or mdc:File.md for MDC-Android docs.
conventions.units: dp for dimensions, sp for text, ms for durations; shapes are [top-start, top-end, bottom-end, bottom-start] dp or "full".

files.describes: All tokens, references resolved, both modes.
The same tokens as a DTCG 2025.10 document with references intact, for theming tools.
Loading indicator morph pairs, pre-matched for linear interpolation.

components.name: Top app bar
components.summary: A horizontal bar anchored to the top of a screen that carries a screen title, primary navigation and up to a few high-priority actions. Pick small for most screens, medium/large (fixed or flexible) when the title needs visual weight or a subtitle, center-aligned for a more formal/branded header, and the search app bar when the screen's primary action is search.

components.name: Badge
components.summary: A small status indicator overlaid on the corner of an icon or navigation item, showing that something changed without interrupting the user. Use a dot for a plain attention signal, a numeral for a short count or label.

components.name: Bottom app bar
components.summary: A bar anchored to the bottom of the screen carrying a handful of frequent actions and, optionally, an embedded FAB. Use the fixed variant for a stable 80dp bar; use the flexible variant when the bar's height or item spacing needs to adapt to its content. MDC-Android recommends the docked toolbar instead for new designs.

components.name: Button
components.summary: A single-action button. Choose emphasis by colour style (filled > elevated ≈ tonal > outlined > text) and choose size by the density of the surrounding layout, not by importance.

components.name: Button group
components.summary: An invisible row container that spaces a set of buttons and adds press interaction between neighbors. Choose standard to keep each button's own shape and support weighted/flexible widths, or connected to fuse them into one pill silhouette as the Expressive replacement for the deprecated segmented button.

components.name: Card
components.summary: A container that groups content and actions about a single subject. Elevated cards separate from the background with a shadow; filled cards use a tonal surface for lower emphasis; outlined cards use a border for the lowest emphasis on backgrounds that already separate content.

components.name: Carousel
components.summary: A horizontal (or vertical) scroller that shows a mix of large, medium, and small items so several pieces of visual content are browsable at once, with items masking/expanding as they scroll toward the edge. Choose it over a standard scroll view when items should snap and change size near the edges.

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: A square selection control for choosing zero, one or many items from a list, or for toggling a single on/off setting when a list-item-style label is present. Prefer switch for a standalone setting with an immediate effect; prefer checkbox for list selection and tri-state (indeterminate) parent/child selection.

components.name: Chips
components.summary: Compact, tappable elements for input, attributes, filtering, or one-off actions. Use assist for a single contextual action, filter for toggling membership in a content set, input for user-entered discrete values, and suggestion for tapping a dynamically generated hint.

components.name: Date picker
components.summary: A modal dialog for choosing a single date, with two interchangeable display modes — a calendar grid and a single free-text field — toggled in place inside the same container. Range selection is a related but separate mode, noted only briefly here.

components.name: Dialog
components.summary: A modal window that interrupts the user for a required decision or critical information. Use it for short, focused prompts; use a bottom sheet instead when the content is a longer list of choices or benefits from swipe dismissal.

components.name: Divider
components.summary: A thin line that groups or separates content in lists and layouts. Purely visual, with no label, icon or interactive behaviour; choose it over extra spacing when a boundary must be explicit.

components.name: Floating action button
components.summary: The single most important action on a screen, floating above content; use one per screen. The extended FAB adds a text label for extra context and can collapse to icon-only on scroll.

components.name: FAB menu
components.summary: A FAB that expands into a vertical list of labelled action items above it. The trigger morphs from a circular add button into a close button as the menu opens.

components.name: Icon button
components.summary: A button whose entire content is a single icon, for compact actions in toolbars, app bars, list rows and cards. Choose the colour style for emphasis and the width option to fit the surrounding layout.

components.name: List
components.summary: A continuous, vertical index of text and/or images. Use a standard list for one/two/three-line rows; use the Expressive additions when rows need to grow inline (expanded-list), be manually reordered (reorder-list), or expose swipe actions (reveal-list).

components.name: Loading indicator
components.summary: An indeterminate, or progress-driven, indicator that morphs a single filled blob through a sequence of Material shapes instead of spinning a ring or filling a bar. Use it in place of the indeterminate circular progress indicator for waits under about 5 seconds; keep the circular progress indicator for longer or unbounded waits.

components.name: Menu
components.summary: A temporary surface listing choices, opened from a button, icon or other anchor. The legacy flat dropdown is a plain list with an optional divider; Expressive menus compose the same items into rounded groups with a standard (surface-tinted) or vibrant (tertiary-tinted) container colour, with a segmented-menu geometry for grouped/selectable items.

components.name: Navigation bar
components.summary: A bottom bar of 3-5 (up to 6 in the flexible variant) top-level destinations, always visible on compact/medium widths. Use it instead of a rail once the window is too narrow to dock navigation to a side.

components.name: Navigation drawer
components.summary: Standard drawers sit alongside content permanently or dismissibly for frequent, deliberate navigation; modal drawers overlay content behind a scrim for infrequent access on compact layouts. MDC-Android marks this component deprecated in Expressive, recommending an expanded navigation rail instead; ship it for parity with existing apps, not for new designs.

components.name: Navigation rail
components.summary: A side-docked bar of 3-7 top-level destinations for tablet/desktop widths. Use collapsed as the default docked state; let it expand in place (or present modally) when the destination set needs labels or the surface plays the role a navigation drawer would on a phone.

components.name: Progress indicator
components.summary: Shows the status of a determinate or indeterminate process as a filled line or ring. Choose plain for a neutral, restrained wait; choose wavy for a more expressive, attention-getting wait, less legible at very small sizes.

components.name: Radio button
components.summary: A circular selection control for choosing exactly one option from a mutually exclusive set. Always used in groups of two or more; never used alone, and never has an indeterminate state.

components.name: Search bar
components.summary: A persistent, pill-shaped entry point for search that expands into a full-screen or docked search view showing suggestions/results. Use the compact bar wherever search is a secondary action in a screen's app bar; the expanded view is a transient state of the same control, not a separate screen the user navigates to.

components.name: Segmented button
components.summary: A row of 2-5 mutually touching outlined buttons sharing one outline, acting as a single- or multi-select choice control. Deprecated in favor of the connected button group, which MDC-Android says has "mostly the same functionality but with an updated visual design"; implement this only to read or author legacy M3 UI.

components.name: Sheets
components.summary: Surfaces anchored to a screen edge that hold supplementary content: bottom sheets rise from the bottom edge, side sheets slide in from left/right. Each has a standard (persistent, no scrim) and modal (blocking, scrimmed) form.

components.name: Slider
components.summary: A one-dimensional control for selecting a value, or a range with two handles, from a continuous or stepped scale. Choose it over a stepper or text input when relative position matters more than the exact number.

components.name: Snackbar
components.summary: A brief, transient message about a process or event, anchored to the bottom of the screen. It never blocks interaction and never requires a response; an action is optional.

components.name: Split button
components.summary: A leading action button fused to a trailing toggle button that opens a menu of related actions. Use it when one action is primary and its alternatives belong in a menu; it is a two-button connected button group with fixed roles.

components.name: Switch
components.summary: A binary on/off control whose effect applies immediately, with no separate save or confirm step. Prefer switch over checkbox for a standalone setting; prefer checkbox for list selection.

components.name: Tab row
components.summary: A horizontal row of tabs that switches between sibling content panes. Use primary tabs (bold, centered indicator) at the top level under an app bar; use secondary tabs (thin underline) to further split content within a section that already has primary navigation.

components.name: Text field
components.summary: A single- or multi-line input for short-to-medium free text. Filled sits on a tinted surface with a bottom indicator line; outlined sits on a transparent background with a full border. Autocomplete composes either variant with a popup menu of selectable options anchored to the field.

components.name: Time picker
components.summary: A modal dialog for choosing an hour and minute, with an optional AM/PM period. It has two interchangeable modes — an analog clock dial and a pair of numeric text fields — toggled in place inside the same container.

components.name: Toolbar
components.summary: A floating toolbar surfaces contextual actions for the content beneath it and can float anywhere on screen, optionally paired with a FAB; a docked toolbar spans the window width with actions that stay constant across pages, replacing the bottom app bar.

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: A small popup that labels or explains an anchor element on hover, long-press, or keyboard focus. Choose plain for a short one-line label; choose rich when the content needs a title, multi-line body, or an action.
